questions.prompt: Why can two magnetic field lines never cross?
options: The field can only have one direction at any point
questions.explain: A compass there would have to point two ways at once.

questions.prompt: Which rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire?
questions.explain: Thumb along the current, fingers show the field.

questions.prompt: How does the field around a straight wire change as you move away from it?
questions.explain: The circles are spaced further apart.

questions.prompt: What is the field like inside a long solenoid?
questions.explain: Like the inside of a bar magnet.

questions.prompt: Which change would make an electromagnet stronger?
questions.explain: More turns and more current both strengthen it.

questions.prompt: A current flows vertically downwards in a wire. Seen from above, the field lines around it go…
questions.explain: Thumb pointing down: fingers curl clockwise seen from above.

questions.prompt: Why is soft iron used for the core of an electromagnet, rather than steel?
options: It keeps its magnetism for ever
It magnetises strongly but loses its magnetism when the current stops
questions.explain: That makes the magnet easy to switch off.

questions.prompt: Describe how a scrap-yard crane uses an electromagnet to lift and drop cars.
questions.modelAnswer: The crane has a large coil wound on a soft iron core. When current flows, the coil and core become a strong magnet that attracts the steel car so it can be lifted. To drop the car, the current is switched off; the soft iron loses its magnetism and the car falls.
rubric: Current on: strong magnet lifts steel
Current off: magnetism lost, car released
